## Overview

On gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X), give the two slowest Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill kernels, `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` and `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64`, gfx942-specific Triton autotune configurations that use the 16×16 MFMA form. The GDN algorithm and kernel arithmetic do not change, and outputs are bit-identical. On MI300X, one GDN prefill layer is 1.34–1.48x faster at 8,192 tokens and 1.24–1.58x faster at 32,768 tokens.

## Claims

- On MI300X, one GDN prefill layer is 1.34–1.48x faster at 8,192 tokens and 1.24–1.58x faster at 32,768 tokens, at the head counts of Qwen3.5/3.8-27B and Qwen3-Next-80B at TP1, and of Qwen3.5-397B and Qwen3-Next-80B at TP8.
- On MI300X at 8,192 tokens with 16 key / 48 value heads, `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` goes from 473.9 to 168.8 µs and `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` from 572.6 to 477.0 µs.
- On MI300X, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 at TP1 had 1.0–2.8% lower median TTFT at every tested input length and concurrency with the first version of this PR, whose layer speedup was smaller (see Validation).
- Output and final recurrent state are bit-identical to the stock configurations.
- Only gfx942 changes. CUDA, other AMD GPUs, and the AITER FlyDSL path selected by `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` keep their configurations.

## Validation

**Environment.** MI300X, one GPU per server or benchmark. Both arms use `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b` (`sha256:009169c114af5b15e25eddc808afb3c1fc3f12c94e746472b16f39fcf39cd716`; vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev157+gedad8b03c, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0). Before is the image as shipped, whose `chunk_o.py` and `chunk_delta_h.py` match this PR's merge base; after mounts this PR's two files over them.

**Kernel level.** One GDN prefill layer: `chunk_gated_delta_rule` called the way `ChunkGatedDeltaRule.forward_native` calls it, one sequence, `triton.testing.do_bench` median. Each run is a fresh process that autotunes once at 64 tokens, as `_warmup_prefill_kernels` does in serving. After: two runs (they agree within 0.9% at 8,192 and 32,768 tokens); before: one run.

| Key / value heads | Model | Tokens | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 / 48 | Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.8-27B (TP1) | 8,192 | 1.562 ms | 1.128 ms | 1.38x |
| | | 32,768 | 6.777 ms | 4.755 ms | 1.43x |
| 16 / 32 | Qwen3-Next-80B (TP1) | 8,192 | 1.213 ms | 0.872 ms | 1.39x |
| | | 32,768 | 4.852 ms | 3.918 ms | 1.24x |
| 2 / 8 | Qwen3.5-397B (TP8) | 8,192 | 0.694 ms | 0.468 ms | 1.48x |
| | | 32,768 | 2.611 ms | 1.781 ms | 1.47x |
| 2 / 4 | Qwen3-Next-80B (TP8) | 8,192 | 0.624 ms | 0.466 ms | 1.34x |
| | | 32,768 | 2.268 ms | 1.435 ms | 1.58x |

At 1,024 tokens the layer is launch-bound and changes by 1.03–1.06x. Output and final state were bit-identical to before at all 24 points.

**Where the time goes.** 16 key / 48 value heads, 8,192 tokens. Device time of each kernel inside the layer (median of 30 calls, L2 flushed before each).

| Kernel | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` | 473.9 µs | 168.8 µs | −305.1 µs |
| `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` | 572.6 µs | 477.0 µs | −95.6 µs |
| Layer (`do_bench` median) | 1.562 ms | 1.128 ms | 1.38x |

<details>
<summary>Each change on its own</summary>

`chunk_fwd_kernel_o` alone on the same 8,192-token inputs, configuration pinned, `do_bench` median (µs). All 219 configurations that compile produce output bit-identical to the before pick's.

| BK / BV | MFMA | `num_warps` | `num_stages` | 16/48 heads | 2/8 heads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 / 32 | 32×32 | 4 | 2 | 498.1 (before pick) | 75.0 |
| 64 / 64 | 32×32 | 4 | 2 | 359.6 | 65.8 |
| 64 / 64 | 32×32 | 4 | 1 | 309.8 | 62.4 |
| 64 / 64 | 16×16 | 4 | 2 | 278.8 | 56.1 |
| 64 / 64 | 16×16 | 4 | 1 | 231.0 | 47.8 |
| 64 / 128 | 16×16 | 4 | 1 | 197.2 (after) | 47.5 |
| 64 / 128 | 16×16 | 2 | 1 | 197.8 (after) | 45.6 |

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` inside the layer, `BV=32`, `num_stages=2`, device time (µs), 8,192 tokens:

| `num_warps` | MFMA | `waves_per_eu` | 16/48 heads | 2/8 heads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 32×32 | 0 | 573.5 (before pick) | 494.8 |
| 8 | 32×32 | 0 | 733.7 | 674.1 |
| 4 | 16×16 | 0 | 502.3 | 384.8 |
| 8 | 16×16 | 0 | 496.3 | 344.2 |
| 8 | 16×16 | 2 | 478.2 (after) | 310.7 (after) |

Every `num_stages=3` variant fails to compile with `OutOfResources: shared memory, Required: 69632` to `81920, Hardware limit: 65536`.

</details>

**End-to-end serving (first version of this PR).** Measured with this PR's first commit (`1eadcb1`), which appended gfx942 candidates to the stock lists and picked `chunk_o BK=64, BV=64` and `chunk_delta_h` without `waves_per_eu`; in the kernel-level harness above its layer speedup at 16/48 heads and 8,192 tokens is 1.32x, against 1.38x now. Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, TP1, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` so the Triton/FLA GDN prefill runs (confirmed in every server log), random prompts, 128 output tokens. Four GPUs each served both arms in turn, alternating which went first, each server from a cold cache. Every point used its own seed, so no prompt repeated within a server. Each value is the mean over the four GPUs of the server's `output_throughput`, `median_ttft_ms` and `median_tpot_ms`; the change is after vs. before.

Higher output tok/s and lower TTFT and TPOT are better.

2,048 input tokens, 128 output tokens

| Concurrency | Prompts | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | After faster (TTFT) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 30.5 → 30.6 (+0.1%) | 331.9 → 328.4 (−1.0%) | 30.39 → 30.36 (−0.1%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |

8,192 input tokens, 128 output tokens

| Concurrency | Prompts | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | After faster (TTFT) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 19.6 → 19.7 (+0.3%) | 1172.3 → 1152.6 (−1.7%) | 42.16 → 42.14 (−0.0%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |
| 2 | 20 | 31.9 → 32.1 (+0.6%) | 2428.4 → 2383.8 (−1.8%) | 43.99 → 43.98 (−0.0%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |
| 4 | 40 | 47.9 → 48.4 (+1.2%) | 4993.3 → 4871.2 (−2.4%) | 44.81 → 44.82 (+0.0%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |
| 8 | 80 | 61.5 → 62.5 (+1.6%) | 7274.8 → 7067.9 (−2.8%) | 73.99 → 73.51 (−0.7%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |
| 32 | 160 | 80.4 → 82.1 (+2.2%) | 10857.5 → 10557.6 (−2.8%) | 314.82 → 307.79 (−2.2%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |

32,768 input tokens, 128 output tokens

| Concurrency | Prompts | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | After faster (TTFT) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 | 7.6 → 7.6 (+0.7%) | 5502.7 → 5385.0 (−2.1%) | 89.49 → 89.47 (−0.0%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |

After was faster in all 28 same-GPU comparisons. TPOT moves only at concurrency 8 and 32, where decode steps often carry prefill chunks; decode itself does not use these kernels. Greedy completions for four fixed prompts were identical on all eight servers.

**Test coverage.** On gfx942, `tests/kernels/fla/test_gdn_gfx942_autotune_configs.py` runs every gfx942 configuration against the stock pick (`chunk_o BK=32, BV=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=2`; `chunk_delta_h BV=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=2`) and requires bit-identical output and final state; `torch.empty` is NaN-filled during those runs, so a configuration that skips a store cannot pass on leftover memory.

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/fla/test_gdn_gfx942_autotune_configs.py
pytest -q tests/kernels/fla
```

On MI300X (gfx942): 3 passed; `tests/kernels/fla` 1658 passed, 22 skipped (fused GDN decode MTP op not built in the image).

## Details

On gfx942 the two kernels get their own configuration lists:

| Kernel | gfx942 configurations |
|---|---|
| `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` | `BK=64, BV=128, matrix_instr_nonkdim=16, num_stages=1`, `num_warps` 2 and 4 |
| `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` | `BV=32, matrix_instr_nonkdim=16, waves_per_eu=2, num_warps=8, num_stages=2` |

- **Use the 16×16 MFMA form.** Without `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`, Triton emits `v_mfma_f32_32x32x8_bf16`. With these kernels' `warpsPerCTA = [2, 2]` layout each warp owns a 32×16 slice of a 64×32 output, so warp pairs compute duplicate 32×32 tiles; the 16×16 form removes that duplicated work in `chunk_delta_h`. In `chunk_o`, the 16×16 accumulator layout reaches the second `tl.dot` through 16-byte `ds_write2st64_b64`/`ds_read2st64_b64` instead of 2-byte `ds_write_b16`/`ds_read_u16`.
- **Wide tile and one stage in `chunk_o`.** `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` recomputes q·kᵀ and re-reads q and k for every BV slice, so the stock pick's `BV=32` does both four times per chunk and head. `check_shared_mem()` uses an NVIDIA-oriented threshold, so gfx942's 64 KB LDS hides 128-wide tiles from the stock list. At `num_stages=2`, Triton keeps the pipelined operands in unswizzled LDS buffers, which cause bank conflicts at the wide tile; with one stage every buffer is swizzled. A sweep of 219 compiling `chunk_o` configurations (BK, BV, `num_warps`, `num_stages`, `waves_per_eu`, MFMA form) found nothing more than 1% faster than `BK=64, BV=128, num_stages=1` at 8,192 and 32,768 tokens. `BK=128` is not used: BK changes the FP32 reduction grouping and the last bits.
- **`waves_per_eu=2` in `chunk_delta_h`.** It caps occupancy so the compiler can give each wave more registers; with `num_warps=8` and the 16×16 form it is 2–20% faster than without it and bit-identical.
- **Why fixed lists rather than appended candidates.** Serving autotunes once at 64 tokens (one chunk), and T is not in the autotune key. With the stock list kept, the 64-token warm-up picked `chunk_o BV=64` in 6 of 6 runs, 17% slower than `BV=128` at 8,192 tokens; lists that leave out `BV=64` fell back to the stock `BK=32, BV=32` pick (2.5x slower) in 5–6 of 6 runs. For `chunk_delta_h`, appending the `waves_per_eu=2` configuration let the warm-up pick the older one at 16/48 heads. Fixed gfx942 lists remove that dependence; the stock lists stay as they are on every other platform. The gfx942 lists have 2 and 1 configurations instead of 36 and 8, so startup autotuning does less work (not re-measured).
- **Compatibility and CI.** `matrix_instr_nonkdim` and `waves_per_eu` are AMD Triton options; vLLM's ROCm MoE path already uses `matrix_instr_nonkdim`. CI runs `tests/kernels/fla` only on B200 and MI355 (gfx950), where the gfx942 tests skip. An optional `:amd: (MI300) FLA gfx942 Autotune Configs` step (`mi300_1`) runs them; like the MI355 FLA job it runs on the scheduled nightly or when unblocked.
- **Related PRs.** #41446 (stale, needs rebase) found the same `chunk_o` tile and uses fixed configurations on all ROCm, bundled with a fused kernel and other changes. With the same kernel source on MI300X, this PR's configurations are 1.5–6.7% faster than #41446's at 16 key heads and 15–29% faster at 2 key heads (8,192 and 32,768 tokens), mostly from `chunk_delta_h` `num_warps=8`; #41446's `kpack=2` also changes the output bits. #43047 prunes configurations that exceed shared memory and adds none.
- **Limits.** KDA models (Kimi Linear, Kimi-K3, GLM-5-Next) also reach the gfx942 `chunk_delta_h` configuration through its `gk` path, which the test does not cover. End-to-end serving was measured with the first version only. Not measured: MI325X performance, serving at TP>1, variable-length batches, and the larger models end to end.

AI assistance was used for the code, tests, measurement scripts, benchmark runs, and this description.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The gfx942 autotune configs added to ``chunk_o`` and ``chunk_delta_h``.
+
+The stock space cannot reach the fastest configuration here: it never sets
+``matrix_instr_nonkdim``, ``chunk_o`` has no ``num_stages=1``, and
+``check_shared_mem()`` compares the device's LDS against a threshold read off a
+table with only NVIDIA entries, so it is ``False`` on gfx942 and the BK/BV=128
+tiles are dropped. These tests pin the properties that make the added configs
+safe: they appear only on gfx942, the installed Triton accepts the backend
+option they rely on, and each one is checked individually against the stock
+result rather than only the one the autotuner happens to choose today.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import triton
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops import chunk_delta_h, chunk_o
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.chunk import chunk_gated_delta_rule
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.utils import check_shared_mem
+
+# A small shape, enough to compile every config and compare results.
+B, T, HG, H, K, V = 1, 1024, 2, 4, 128, 128
+
+# Whether an added config *wins* depends on the head count far more than on the
+# sequence length: at HG=2/H=4 the grid is a few workgroups, the kernels are
+# latency-bound and the whole space is flat, so the autotuner's pick there is
+# noise. Measured on MI325X, stock vs. the full space:
+#
+#     T=1024 HG=2  H=4    1.1526 -> 1.3715 ms   0.840x   no added config won
+#     T=4096 HG=2  H=4    1.8668 -> 2.3300 ms   0.801x   no added config won
+#     T=8192 HG=2  H=4    4.6301 -> 5.4293 ms   0.853x   no added config won
+#     T=4096 HG=16 H=48   2.4262 -> 2.2095 ms   1.098x   added config won
+#     T=8192 HG=16 H=48   6.5200 -> 4.0948 ms   1.592x   added config won
+#
+# So the selection test uses Qwen3-Next's head counts. At T=8192 the margin is
+# 1.592x, far outside the run-to-run spread, which is what makes that assertion
+# safe to make in a test.
+SELECT_T, SELECT_HG, SELECT_H = 8192, 16, 48
+
+
+def _on_gfx942() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    return on_gfx942()
+
+
+def _autotuner(kernel):
+    """Unwrap the triton.heuristics layers down to the Autotuner."""
+    seen = kernel
+    while not hasattr(kernel, "configs"):
+        kernel = getattr(kernel, "fn", None)
+        if kernel is None:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"no triton.Autotuner under {seen!r}; the decorator stack on this "
+                "kernel changed and these tests need updating"
+            )
+    return kernel
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _configs(kernel, configs):
+    """Run with the autotuner restricted to ``configs``, then put it back."""
+    tuner = _autotuner(kernel)
+    saved_configs, saved_cache = tuner.configs, dict(tuner.cache)
+    tuner.configs = configs
+    tuner.cache.clear()
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        tuner.configs = saved_configs
+        tuner.cache.clear()
+        tuner.cache.update(saved_cache)
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _fresh_cache(kernel):
+    """Autotune from scratch over the full space, then put the cache back."""
+    tuner = _autotuner(kernel)
+    saved_cache = dict(tuner.cache)
+    tuner.cache.clear()
+    try:
+        yield tuner
+    finally:
+        tuner.cache.clear()
+        tuner.cache.update(saved_cache)
+
+
+def _added(kernel):
+    return [c for c in _autotuner(kernel).configs if "matrix_instr_nonkdim" in c.kwargs]
+
+
+def _stock(kernel):
+    return [
+        c for c in _autotuner(kernel).configs if "matrix_instr_nonkdim" not in c.kwargs
+    ]
+
+
+def test_configs_are_added_only_on_gfx942():
+    for module in (chunk_o, chunk_delta_h):
+        assert bool(module._GFX942_CONFIGS) == _on_gfx942()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _on_gfx942(), reason="gfx942-specific configs")
+def test_triton_accepts_the_backend_option_the_configs_rely_on():
+    """``matrix_instr_nonkdim`` is a backend option, not a kernel argument.
+
+    Triton's AMD backend lifts it out of the config kwargs at compile time. A
+    Triton that does not recognize it raises rather than being skipped -- the
+    autotuner only swallows ``OutOfResources`` -- so every GDN prefill on gfx942
+    would fail at the first autotune. This test names that dependency, so the
+    failure arrives here with an explanation instead of at a model launch.
+    """
+    kernel = chunk_o.chunk_fwd_kernel_o
+    one_added = _added(kernel)[:1]
+    assert one_added, "no added configs to compile"
+
+    # Restricting the space to a single added config makes this a compile of that
+    # config and nothing else, so a failure here is about the option.
+    with _configs(kernel, one_added):
+        chunk_gated_delta_rule(**_inputs("cuda"))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _on_gfx942(), reason="gfx942-specific configs")
+def test_added_configs_restore_the_tile_the_shared_memory_gate_hides():
+    # The premise of the change: check_shared_mem() measures the device's LDS
+    # against a threshold taken from a table with only NVIDIA entries, so it is
+    # False on gfx942 and the stock space tops out below 128. These tiles win the
+    # isolated long-sequence benchmark; at a served chunk size the autotuner
+    # prefers a stock tile with the MFMA width.
+    #
+    # The gate's value is upstream's to change -- a fix there would be an
+    # improvement, not a regression -- so it is reported, not asserted. What is
+    # asserted is the part this change owns: the wide tile is reachable only
+    # through the configs added here.
+    if check_shared_mem():
+        pytest.skip(
+            "check_shared_mem() is now True on gfx942: upstream's threshold "
+            "changed and the stock space already carries the 128-wide tiles, so "
+            "this test's premise is stale"
+        )
+    assert chunk_o.BKV_LIST == [32, 64]
+
+    stock_tiles = {
+        (c.kwargs["BK"], c.kwargs["BV"]) for c in _stock(chunk_o.chunk_fwd_kernel_o)
+    }
+    added_tiles = {
+        (c.kwargs["BK"], c.kwargs["BV"]) for c in _added(chunk_o.chunk_fwd_kernel_o)
+    }
+    assert (64, 128) not in stock_tiles
+    assert (64, 128) in added_tiles
+
+    # chunk_delta_h keeps its tile and stage count. What the stock space cannot

detail.body:
## Overview

On gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X), give the two slowest Gated DeltaNet (GDN) prefill kernels, `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` and `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64`, gfx942-specific Triton autotune configurations that use the 16×16 MFMA form. The GDN algorithm and kernel arithmetic do not change, and outputs are bit-identical. On MI300X, one GDN prefill layer is 1.34–1.48x faster at 8,192 tokens and 1.24–1.58x faster at 32,768 tokens.

## Claims

- On MI300X, one GDN prefill layer is 1.34–1.48x faster at 8,192 tokens and 1.24–1.58x faster at 32,768 tokens, at the head counts of Qwen3.5/3.8-27B and Qwen3-Next-80B at TP1, and of Qwen3.5-397B and Qwen3-Next-80B at TP8.
- On MI300X at 8,192 tokens with 16 key / 48 value heads, `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` goes from 473.9 to 168.8 µs and `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` from 572.6 to 477.0 µs.
- On MI300X, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 at TP1 had 1.0–2.8% lower median TTFT at every tested input length and concurrency with the first version of this PR, whose layer speedup was smaller (see Validation).
- Output and final recurrent state are bit-identical to the stock configurations.
- Only gfx942 changes. CUDA, other AMD GPUs, and the AITER FlyDSL path selected by `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` keep their configurations.

## Validation

**Environment.** MI300X, one GPU per server or benchmark. Both arms use `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b` (`sha256:009169c114af5b15e25eddc808afb3c1fc3f12c94e746472b16f39fcf39cd716`; vLLM 0.33.0rc1.dev157+gedad8b03c, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0). Before is the image as shipped, whose `chunk_o.py` and `chunk_delta_h.py` match this PR's merge base; after mounts this PR's two files over them.

**Kernel level.** One GDN prefill layer: `chunk_gated_delta_rule` called the way `ChunkGatedDeltaRule.forward_native` calls it, one sequence, `triton.testing.do_bench` median. Each run is a fresh process that autotunes once at 64 tokens, as `_warmup_prefill_kernels` does in serving. After: two runs (they agree within 0.9% at 8,192 and 32,768 tokens); before: one run.

| Key / value heads | Model | Tokens | Before | After | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 / 48 | Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.8-27B (TP1) | 8,192 | 1.562 ms | 1.128 ms | 1.38x |
| | | 32,768 | 6.777 ms | 4.755 ms | 1.43x |
| 16 / 32 | Qwen3-Next-80B (TP1) | 8,192 | 1.213 ms | 0.872 ms | 1.39x |
| | | 32,768 | 4.852 ms | 3.918 ms | 1.24x |
| 2 / 8 | Qwen3.5-397B (TP8) | 8,192 | 0.694 ms | 0.468 ms | 1.48x |
| | | 32,768 | 2.611 ms | 1.781 ms | 1.47x |
| 2 / 4 | Qwen3-Next-80B (TP8) | 8,192 | 0.624 ms | 0.466 ms | 1.34x |
| | | 32,768 | 2.268 ms | 1.435 ms | 1.58x |

At 1,024 tokens the layer is launch-bound and changes by 1.03–1.06x. Output and final state were bit-identical to before at all 24 points.

**Where the time goes.** 16 key / 48 value heads, 8,192 tokens. Device time of each kernel inside the layer (median of 30 calls, L2 flushed before each).

| Kernel | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` | 473.9 µs | 168.8 µs | −305.1 µs |
| `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` | 572.6 µs | 477.0 µs | −95.6 µs |
| Layer (`do_bench` median) | 1.562 ms | 1.128 ms | 1.38x |

<details>
<summary>Each change on its own</summary>

`chunk_fwd_kernel_o` alone on the same 8,192-token inputs, configuration pinned, `do_bench` median (µs). All 219 configurations that compile produce output bit-identical to the before pick's.

| BK / BV | MFMA | `num_warps` | `num_stages` | 16/48 heads | 2/8 heads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 / 32 | 32×32 | 4 | 2 | 498.1 (before pick) | 75.0 |
| 64 / 64 | 32×32 | 4 | 2 | 359.6 | 65.8 |
| 64 / 64 | 32×32 | 4 | 1 | 309.8 | 62.4 |
| 64 / 64 | 16×16 | 4 | 2 | 278.8 | 56.1 |
| 64 / 64 | 16×16 | 4 | 1 | 231.0 | 47.8 |
| 64 / 128 | 16×16 | 4 | 1 | 197.2 (after) | 47.5 |
| 64 / 128 | 16×16 | 2 | 1 | 197.8 (after) | 45.6 |

`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` inside the layer, `BV=32`, `num_stages=2`, device time (µs), 8,192 tokens:

| `num_warps` | MFMA | `waves_per_eu` | 16/48 heads | 2/8 heads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 32×32 | 0 | 573.5 (before pick) | 494.8 |
| 8 | 32×32 | 0 | 733.7 | 674.1 |
| 4 | 16×16 | 0 | 502.3 | 384.8 |
| 8 | 16×16 | 0 | 496.3 | 344.2 |
| 8 | 16×16 | 2 | 478.2 (after) | 310.7 (after) |

Every `num_stages=3` variant fails to compile with `OutOfResources: shared memory, Required: 69632` to `81920, Hardware limit: 65536`.

</details>

**End-to-end serving (first version of this PR).** Measured with this PR's first commit (`1eadcb1`), which appended gfx942 candidates to the stock lists and picked `chunk_o BK=64, BV=64` and `chunk_delta_h` without `waves_per_eu`; in the kernel-level harness above its layer speedup at 16/48 heads and 8,192 tokens is 1.32x, against 1.38x now. Four GPUs each served both arms in turn, alternating which went first, each server from a cold cache. Every point used its own seed, so no prompt repeated within a server. Each value is the mean over the four GPUs of the server's `output_throughput`, `median_ttft_ms` and `median_tpot_ms`; the change is after vs. before.

Higher output tok/s and lower TTFT and TPOT are better.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

8,192 input tokens, 128 output tokens

| Concurrency | Prompts | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | After faster (TTFT) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 19.6 → 19.7 (+0.3%) | 1172.3 → 1152.6 (−1.7%) | 42.16 → 42.14 (−0.0%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |

32,768 input tokens, 128 output tokens

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 | 7.6 → 7.6 (+0.7%) | 5502.7 → 5385.0 (−2.1%) | 89.49 → 89.47 (−0.0%) | 4 of 4 GPUs |

After was faster in all 28 same-GPU comparisons. TPOT moves only at concurrency 8 and 32, where decode steps often carry prefill chunks; decode itself does not use these kernels. Greedy completions for four fixed prompts were identical on all eight servers.

**Test coverage.** On gfx942, `tests/kernels/fla/test_gdn_gfx942_autotune_configs.py` runs every gfx942 configuration against the stock pick (`chunk_o BK=32, BV=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=2`; `chunk_delta_h BV=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=2`) and requires bit-identical output and final state; `torch.empty` is NaN-filled during those runs, so a configuration that skips a store cannot pass on leftover memory.

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/fla/test_gdn_gfx942_autotune_configs.py

```

On MI300X (gfx942): 3 passed; `tests/kernels/fla` 1658 passed, 22 skipped (fused GDN decode MTP op not built in the image).

## Details

On gfx942 the two kernels get their own configuration lists:

| Kernel | gfx942 configurations |
|---|---|
| `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` | `BK=64, BV=128, matrix_instr_nonkdim=16, num_stages=1`, `num_warps` 2 and 4 |
| `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` | `BV=32, matrix_instr_nonkdim=16, waves_per_eu=2, num_warps=8, num_stages=2` |

- **Use the 16×16 MFMA form.** Without `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`, Triton emits `v_mfma_f32_32x32x8_bf16`. With these kernels' `warpsPerCTA = [2, 2]` layout each warp owns a 32×16 slice of a 64×32 output, so warp pairs compute duplicate 32×32 tiles; the 16×16 form removes that duplicated work in `chunk_delta_h`. In `chunk_o`, the 16×16 accumulator layout reaches the second `tl.dot` through 16-byte `ds_write2st64_b64`/`ds_read2st64_b64` instead of 2-byte `ds_write_b16`/`ds_read_u16`.
- **Wide tile and one stage in `chunk_o`.** `chunk_fwd_kernel_o` recomputes q·kᵀ and re-reads q and k for every BV slice, so the stock pick's `BV=32` does both four times per chunk and head. `check_shared_mem()` uses an NVIDIA-oriented threshold, so gfx942's 64 KB LDS hides 128-wide tiles from the stock list. At `num_stages=2`, Triton keeps the pipelined operands in unswizzled LDS buffers, which cause bank conflicts at the wide tile; with one stage every buffer is swizzled. A sweep of 219 compiling `chunk_o` configurations (BK, BV, `num_warps`, `num_stages`, `waves_per_eu`, MFMA form) found nothing more than 1% faster than `BK=64, BV=128, num_stages=1` at 8,192 and 32,768 tokens. `BK=128` is not used: BK changes the FP32 reduction grouping and the last bits.
- **`waves_per_eu=2` in `chunk_delta_h`.** It caps occupancy so the compiler can give each wave more registers; with `num_warps=8` and the 16×16 form it is 2–20% faster than without it and bit-identical.
- **Why fixed lists rather than appended candidates.** Serving autotunes once at 64 tokens (one chunk), and T is not in the autotune key. With the stock list kept, the 64-token warm-up picked `chunk_o BV=64` in 6 of 6 runs, 17% slower than `BV=128` at 8,192 tokens; lists that leave out `BV=64` fell back to the stock `BK=32, BV=32` pick (2.5x slower) in 5–6 of 6 runs. For `chunk_delta_h`, appending the `waves_per_eu=2` configuration let the warm-up pick the older one at 16/48 heads. Fixed gfx942 lists remove that dependence; the stock lists stay as they are on every other platform. The gfx942 lists have 2 and 1 configurations instead of 36 and 8, so startup autotuning does less work (not re-measured).
- **Compatibility and CI.** `matrix_instr_nonkdim` and `waves_per_eu` are AMD Triton options; vLLM's ROCm MoE path already uses `matrix_instr_nonkdim`. CI runs `tests/kernels/fla` only on B200 and MI355 (gfx950), where the gfx942 tests skip. An optional `:amd: (MI300) FLA gfx942 Autotune Configs` step (`mi300_1`) runs them; like the MI355 FLA job it runs on the scheduled nightly or when unblocked.
- **Related PRs.** #41446 (stale, needs rebase) found the same `chunk_o` tile and uses fixed configurations on all ROCm, bundled with a fused kernel and other changes. With the same kernel source on MI300X, this PR's configurations are 1.5–6.7% faster than #41446's at 16 key heads and 15–29% faster at 2 key heads (8,192 and 32,768 tokens), mostly from `chunk_delta_h` `num_warps=8`; #41446's `kpack=2` also changes the output bits. #43047 prunes configurations that exceed shared memory and adds none.
- **Limits.** KDA models (Kimi Linear, Kimi-K3, GLM-5-Next) also reach the gfx942 `chunk_delta_h` configuration through its `gk` path, which the test does not cover. End-to-end serving was measured with the first version only. Not measured: MI325X performance, serving at TP>1, variable-length batches, and the larger models end to end.

+"""The gfx942 autotune configs added to ``chunk_o`` and ``chunk_delta_h``.
+
+The stock space cannot reach the fastest configuration here: it never sets
+``matrix_instr_nonkdim``, ``chunk_o`` has no ``num_stages=1``, and
+``check_shared_mem()`` compares the device's LDS against a threshold read off a
+table with only NVIDIA entries, so it is ``False`` on gfx942 and the BK/BV=128
+tiles are dropped. These tests pin the properties that make the added configs
+safe: they appear only on gfx942, the installed Triton accepts the backend
+option they rely on, and each one is checked individually against the stock
+result rather than only the one the autotuner happens to choose today.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import triton
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops import chunk_delta_h, chunk_o
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.chunk import chunk_gated_delta_rule
+from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.utils import check_shared_mem
+
+# A small shape, enough to compile every config and compare results.
+B, T, HG, H, K, V = 1, 1024, 2, 4, 128, 128
+
+# Whether an added config *wins* depends on the head count far more than on the
+# sequence length: at HG=2/H=4 the grid is a few workgroups, the kernels are
+# latency-bound and the whole space is flat, so the autotuner's pick there is
+# noise. Measured on MI325X, stock vs. the full space:
+#
+#     T=1024 HG=2  H=4    1.1526 -> 1.3715 ms   0.840x   no added config won
+#     T=4096 HG=2  H=4    1.8668 -> 2.3300 ms   0.801x   no added config won
+#     T=8192 HG=2  H=4    4.6301 -> 5.4293 ms   0.853x   no added config won
+#     T=4096 HG=16 H=48   2.4262 -> 2.2095 ms   1.098x   added config won
+#     T=8192 HG=16 H=48   6.5200 -> 4.0948 ms   1.592x   added config won
+#
+# So the selection test uses Qwen3-Next's head counts. At T=8192 the margin is
+# 1.592x, far outside the run-to-run spread, which is what makes that assertion
+# safe to make in a test.
+SELECT_T, SELECT_HG, SELECT_H = 8192, 16, 48
+
+
+def _on_gfx942() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx942
+
+    return on_gfx942()
+
+
+def _autotuner(kernel):
+    """Unwrap the triton.heuristics layers down to the Autotuner."""
+    seen = kernel
+    while not hasattr(kernel, "configs"):
+        kernel = getattr(kernel, "fn", None)
+        if kernel is None:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"no triton.Autotuner under {seen!r}; the decorator stack on this "
+                "kernel changed and these tests need updating"
+            )
+    return kernel
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _configs(kernel, configs):
+    """Run with the autotuner restricted to ``configs``, then put it back."""
+    tuner = _autotuner(kernel)
+    saved_configs, saved_cache = tuner.configs, dict(tuner.cache)
+    tuner.configs = configs
+    tuner.cache.clear()
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        tuner.configs = saved_configs
+        tuner.cache.clear()
+        tuner.cache.update(saved_cache)
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _fresh_cache(kernel):
+    """Autotune from scratch over the full space, then put the cache back."""
+    tuner = _autotuner(kernel)
+    saved_cache = dict(tuner.cache)
+    tuner.cache.clear()
+    try:
+        yield tuner
+    finally:
+        tuner.cache.clear()
+        tuner.cache.update(saved_cache)
+
+
+def _added(kernel):
+    return [c for c in _autotuner(kernel).configs if "matrix_instr_nonkdim" in c.kwargs]
+
+
+def _stock(kernel):
+    return [
+        c for c in _autotuner(kernel).configs if "matrix_instr_nonkdim" not in c.kwargs
+    ]
+
+
+def test_configs_are_added_only_on_gfx942():
+    for module in (chunk_o, chunk_delta_h):
+        assert bool(module._GFX942_CONFIGS) == _on_gfx942()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _on_gfx942(), reason="gfx942-specific configs")
+def test_triton_accepts_the_backend_option_the_configs_rely_on():
+    """``matrix_instr_nonkdim`` is a backend option, not a kernel argument.
+
+    Triton's AMD backend lifts it out of the config kwargs at compile time. A
+    Triton that does not recognize it raises rather than being skipped -- the
+    autotuner only swallows ``OutOfResources`` -- so every GDN prefill on gfx942
+    would fail at the first autotune. This test names that dependency, so the
+    failure arrives here with an explanation instead of at a model launch.
+    """
+    kernel = chunk_o.chunk_fwd_kernel_o
+    one_added = _added(kernel)[:1]
+    assert one_added, "no added configs to compile"
+
+    # Restricting the space to a single added config makes this a compile of that
+    # config and nothing else, so a failure here is about the option.
+    with _configs(kernel, one_added):
+        chunk_gated_delta_rule(**_inputs("cuda"))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _on_gfx942(), reason="gfx942-specific configs")
+def test_added_configs_restore_the_tile_the_shared_memory_gate_hides():
+    # The premise of the change: check_shared_mem() measures the device's LDS
+    # against a threshold taken from a table with only NVIDIA entries, so it is
+    # False on gfx942 and the stock space tops out below 128. These tiles win the
+    # isolated long-sequence benchmark; at a served chunk size the autotuner
+    # prefers a stock tile with the MFMA width.
+    #
+    # The gate's value is upstream's to change -- a fix there would be an
+    # improvement, not a regression -- so it is reported, not asserted. What is
+    # asserted is the part this change owns: the wide tile is reachable only
+    # through the configs added here.
+    if check_shared_mem():
+        pytest.skip(
+            "check_shared_mem() is now True on gfx942: upstream's threshold "
+            "changed and the stock space already carries the 128-wide tiles, so "
+            "this test's premise is stale"
+        )
+    assert chunk_o.BKV_LIST == [32, 64]

+        (c.kwargs["BK"], c.kwargs["BV"]) for c in _stock(chunk_o.chunk_fwd_kernel_o)

+        (c.kwargs["BK"], c.kwargs["BV"]) for c in _added(chunk_o.chunk_fwd_kernel_o)

+    # reach is the MFMA width and, only in combination with it, num_warps=8 --
+    # the warp extension on its own measures 0.982x, slightly slower.
+    kernel = chunk_delta_h.chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64
+    assert max(c.num_warps for c in _stock(kernel)) == 4
+    assert max(c.num_warps for c in _added(kernel)) == 8
+
+

+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    return dict(
+        q=torch.randn(B, t, hg, K, dtype=dtype, device=device),
+        k=torch.nn.functional.normalize(
+            torch.randn(B, t, hg, K, dtype=dtype, device=device), p=2, dim=-1
+        ),
+        v=torch.randn(B, t, h, V, dtype=dtype, device=device),
+        g=torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(
+            torch.rand(B, t, h, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        ),
+        beta=torch.rand(B, t, h, dtype=dtype, device=device).sigmoid(),
+        initial_state=torch.zeros(B, h, K, V, dtype=torch.float32, device=device),
+        output_final_state=True,
+        cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, t], dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+    )
+
+
+_KERNEL_O = "chunk_fwd_kernel_o"
+_KERNEL_H = "chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64"
+
+
+def _kernels():
+    return (
+        chunk_o.chunk_fwd_kernel_o,
+        getattr(chunk_delta_h, _KERNEL_H),
+    )
+
+
+def _pinned(inputs, o_config, h_config):
+    """Run with exactly one config pinned per kernel.
+
+    Returns ``None`` when the config does not fit in LDS. The autotuner swallows
+    exactly that error, so such a config is unreachable in production and is not
+    this test's business; pinning it is what makes it visible.
+    """
+    kernel_o, kernel_h = _kernels()
+    try:
+        with _configs(kernel_o, [o_config]), _configs(kernel_h, [h_config]):
+            out, state = chunk_gated_delta_rule(**inputs)
+    except triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources:
+        return None
+    return out.clone(), state.clone()
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def stock_reference():
+    """Inputs and the stock space's result, as the baseline for every config."""
+    inputs = _inputs("cuda")
+    kernel_o, kernel_h = _kernels()
+    got = _pinned(inputs, _stock(kernel_o)[0], _stock(kernel_h)[0])
+    assert got is not None, "the stock reference config does not fit in LDS"
+    return inputs, got[0], got[1]
+
+
+def _added_cases():
+    """(kernel, config) for every added config, or [] off gfx942."""
+    if not _on_gfx942():
+        return []
+    kernel_o, kernel_h = _kernels()
+    return [(_KERNEL_O, c) for c in _added(kernel_o)] + [
+        (_KERNEL_H, c) for c in _added(kernel_h)
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _on_gfx942(), reason="gfx942-specific configs")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "kernel_name,config", _added_cases(), ids=lambda v: str(v).replace(" ", "")
+)
+def test_added_config_matches_the_stock_result(kernel_name, config, stock_reference):
+    """Every added config, checked individually against the stock result.
+
+    Bit-identity is measured, not guaranteed: a config is a scheduling choice,
+    but BK is the K-loop tile, so changing it would re-associate an fp32
+    reduction. Every config added here keeps the stock BK, and all of them are
+    bit-identical on MI325X. A BK=128 family was measured and left out for
+    exactly this reason -- it differs in the last bits of a handful of elements.
+
+    Asserting it per config is the point: whether the end-to-end result is
+    bit-identical depends otherwise on which config the autotuner picks for the
+    shape under test, which is not a property of this change.
+    """
+    inputs, ref_out, ref_state = stock_reference
+    kernel_o, kernel_h = _kernels()
+    if kernel_name == _KERNEL_O:
+        got = _pinned(inputs, config, _stock(kernel_h)[0])
+    else:
+        got = _pinned(inputs, _stock(kernel_o)[0], config)
+    if got is None:
+        pytest.skip(f"{config} does not fit in LDS; the autotuner skips it too")
+    out, state = got
+
+    # The recurrent state is carried across chunks, so it must match exactly for
+    # every config -- a difference there would compound down the sequence.
+    assert torch.equal(ref_state, state), f"final state changed under {config}"
+    assert torch.equal(ref_out, out), f"output changed under {config}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _on_gfx942(), reason="gfx942-specific configs")

+#     T=1024 HG=2  H=4    1.1526 -> 1.3715 ms   0.840x   no added config won

+
+
+def _autotuner(kernel):
+    """Unwrap the triton.heuristics layers down to the Autotuner."""
+    seen = kernel
+    while not hasattr(kernel, "configs"):
+        kernel = getattr(kernel, "fn", None)

+    tuner.cache.clear()

+    # against a threshold taken from a table with only NVIDIA entries, so it is

+    # prefers a stock tile with the MFMA width.

+    # asserted is the part this change owns: the wide tile is reachable only
+    # through the configs added here.

+        pytest.skip(
+            "check_shared_mem() is now True on gfx942: upstream's threshold "
+            "changed and the stock space already carries the 128-wide tiles, so "
+            "this test's premise is stale"
+        )

+
